subject.title: Windows: multiple gateway-down failure modes (kill-and-rebind restart loop, config-edit no-relaunch, browser launch crash, blocking pricing fetches)

question: Should this issue remain the canonical Windows gateway-down umbrella while maintainers split separate fixes for lifecycle, invalid-config repair, Browser plugin isolation, pricing readiness, and Claude CLI shim behavior?
rationale: The report combines credible failures across stable gateway/runtime boundaries, and the right split, recovery UX, and live-proof order require maintainer ownership rather than one autonomous patch.

options.title: Keep Umbrella And Split Fixes
options.body: Use this issue as the incident tracker and create or link narrow maintainer-owned fixes for each proven sub-boundary.

options.title: Require Live Windows Proof First
options.body: Pause implementation until a maintainer or reporter captures process, listener, browser, and startup timing proof for the highest-risk paths.

options.title: Track Only Narrow Canonicals
options.body: Move each surviving subproblem to its narrower related issue and close this umbrella only after the links preserve all unique evidence.

recommendation.title: Keep Umbrella And Split Fixes
recommendation.body: Use this issue as the incident tracker and create or link narrow maintainer-owned fixes for each proven sub-boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest current-main history across the gateway lifecycle, process cleanup, pricing, browser launch, and Windows spawn surfaces touched by the report.
